A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MatAnyone and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices G–J. The complete supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MatAnyone benchmark results and ablations in Tables 1–3, with additional qualitative experiments in Appendix J.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative experimental results, including revised numerical results in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: V2 removes the optional auxiliary-free inference variant described in v1 Section 3.3, which initializes MatAnyone using a binarized first-frame alpha prediction from RVM. The principal architecture, consistent memory propagation, losses, training strategy, and recurrent refinement remain unchanged.

E1.justification: All datasets and general/instance matting coverage remain. However, removing Ours-AF from Table 1 eliminates evaluation of MatAnyone without an externally supplied target mask on VideoMatte and YouTubeMatte, narrowing its tested input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes Ours-AF from the evaluated comparison set. The external comparators MODNet, RVM, RVM-Large, AdaM, FTP-VM, and MaGGIe remain, as do the appendix comparisons, including Matte Anything.

E3.justification: The RVM-initialized Ours-AF comparison is removed, eliminating a control using RVM-derived first-frame guidance. The retained experiments keep their stated resolutions, metrics, training schedules, and real-world sample selection. No stated protocol revision explains the updated scores.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix J retain the same ablations of training data, memory propagation, core supervision, scaled DDC loss, and recurrent refinement. The harmonization demonstration, challenging video cases, and qualitative analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results without experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Repeating the first frame is an inference procedure, not repeated-run statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 removes Ours-AF results and revises all Ours scores plus RVM-Large's four YouTubeMatte 1080p scores. For example, Ours VideoMatte MAD changes from 5.07 to 5.15 at low resolution and 4.27 to 4.24 at 1080p. Its 1080p Grad changes from 4.04 to 4.00, overtaking MaGGIe's unchanged 4.03. Table 2 changes Ours MAD/MSE/dtSSD from 0.18/0.11/0.95 to 0.14/0.10/0.89. The principal findings remain similar.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and equations remain unchanged, including memory fusion, the scaled DDC derivation in Section 3.2, and the attention and loss formulations in appendices G–H.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about target-assigned matting, consistent memory propagation, improved datasets, and segmentation-based supervision. The removed auxiliary-free variant was a secondary extension.

C2.justification: Section 5.1.1 removes the argument that improvements over RVM persist with RVM-derived initialization. It instead emphasizes the main method's best connectivity scores as evidence of visual quality. The other mechanism explanations, applicability discussion, and qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The demo-video hyperlink in Appendix J.6 changes to a different YouTube video identifier despite unchanged visible text. This changes access information; the PDFs do not establish the linked video's contents or availability. Architecture, hyperparameters, augmentation instructions, and dataset-generation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds ProPainter, cited as reference 60, to Section 2's discussion of optical-flow-guided propagation for video consistency. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; subsequent reference-number shifts reflect this addition.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 is retitled Recurrent Refinement During Inference, with corresponding overview and contents edits. V2 also makes limited grammatical and discussion edits and adds a funding acknowledgement. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 loses the Ours-AF column and redistributes column widths. Tables and nearby paragraphs undergo limited repositioning and page reflow. The figure content is retained, and appendix pages 12–22 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: V1's RVM-initialized Ours-AF results support comparison with RVM without externally supplied target guidance. V2 removes this useful evidence while retaining comparisons against auxiliary-free methods. The editorial improvements and revised scores provide no clear replacement validation. The unchanged core method and extensive retained ablations keep this loss in evidential support limited.
